title: _aggregate_v2_build_response and _aggregate_v2_status_response duplicate an identical ~28-line per-port aggregation core
description: The two functions share a byte-identical aggregation body that walks `tables`, sums `row_count`/`column_count`, accumulates `size_bytes` and `cached_at` from each table's on-disk parquet stat, and builds the synthetic `columns` map. The only real differences are: (a) the input variable name (`summary` vs `meta`), (b) the `skipped` access style (strict `summary["skipped"]` vs tolerant `meta.get("skipped") or {}`), and (c) the response wrapper (build adds `cache_seconds`, status sets `cached=True`). The shared core can be extracted into one helper (e.g. `_aggregate_v2_tables(cache_dir, tables) -> (row_count, column_count, columns, size_bytes, cached_at)`), with each caller adding only its differing fields. This removes a two-way drift hazard in a cache-integrity hot path where the build and status responses are contractually required to report the same row/column/size numbers for the same cache.
evidence: Lines 268-284 (build) and 312-328 (status) are identical apart from the receiver name: `tables = X.get("tables", []) or []`; `row_count = sum(int(t.get("row_count", 0)) for t in tables)`; `column_count = sum(int(t.get("column_count", 0)) for t in tables)`; identical `for table in tables:` loop computing `label`, `parquet_name`, `parquet_path = cache_dir / parquet_name`, `if parquet_path.exists(): stat = parquet_path.stat(); size_bytes += int(stat.st_size); cached_at = max(cached_at, float(stat.st_mtime))`; identical `for ci in range(int(table.get("column_count", 0))): columns[f"{label}.col{ci}"] = "v2"`. Only the `skipped` line and the final return object differ.
est_reduction: ~28 LOC of duplicated aggregation collapsed to one shared helper; eliminates a build-vs-status divergence hazard.
behavior_preservation: The extracted helper reproduces the same iteration order, the same int()/float() coercions, the same `isinstance(parquet_name, str)` and `.exists()` guards, and the same `{label}.colN` key construction; each wrapper keeps its own strict/tolerant `skipped` read and its own response type and extra fields (`cache_seconds`, `cached=True`). Output is identical for every input.
